name: Cursor
summary: A VS Code fork built around editing whole files with a model, rather than completing one line at a time.
description:
Cursor takes the editor shell people already know and rebuilds the parts around it: a diff-based multi-file edit flow, a codebase index that answers "where is this handled" questions, and an agent mode that runs commands and iterates on failures. The reason developers stick with it is the review loop — edits land as diffs you can accept chunk by chunk, which is very different from pasting a model's output into a file and hoping.

Where it gets expensive is the same place it gets good: multi-file agent runs burn tokens quickly, and a long session against a large repository can quietly consume a week of free-request allowance. It is also a fork, so you are taking the vendor's extension compatibility and update cadence rather than upstream VS Code's, and enterprise policy teams tend to notice that before the developers do.
